library.name: note-cpp

library.sentence: Typed C++ SDK for the Blues Notecard.
library.paragraph: Type-safe, compile-time checked API for all Notecard endpoints. Header-only. Supports Arduino, PlatformIO, and CMake.

library.name: tarfs
library.author: Viacheslav Logunov <vvb333007@gmail.com>
library.sentence: High-performance immutable TAR filesystem for ESP32 with mmap().
library.paragraph: Memory-efficient read-only TAR filesystem with zero-copy mmap(), POSIX-compatible API, hard links, symbolic links, long filenames, UTF-8, CRC64 integrity checking, and low RAM overhead.

library.name: WCB_Client
library.author: Greg Hulette
library.sentence: Client library for joining a Wireless Communication Board (WCB) ESP-NOW network.
library.paragraph: Allows any ESP32-based device to participate as a native peer in a WCB network. Supports unicast and broadcast text commands with automatic fragmentation for long commands (e.g. saving large stored sequences), raw binary forwarding for Pololu/Maestro servo packets via WCBStream, ETM heartbeat and ACK tracking, board online/offline status callbacks, and communication with an out-of-band special peer such as NaviCore via enableSpecialPeer(). A raw-packet hook (onRawPacket/sendRawPacket) lets custom protocols — such as firmware OTA — ride the same ESP-NOW mesh. setIdentity() advertises the device over WDP so WCBs discover it by name and firmware version automatically (the mesh twin of the serial WDP-DA device-announce model), and onNeighbor()/getNeighbor() consume the same WDP adverts to learn every WCB and client on the mesh — alias, firmware, capabilities, controller link and Maestro IDs. With auto-join (on by default) the device also registers regular WCBs it hears as ESP-NOW peers live and remembers them across reboots, so it discovers the fleet once and never needs wcb_quantity to cover it.
